title: Outputs of a full-adder circuit
statement: Let $v$ be a Boolean list of length $L$, and let $a,b,c<L$ be indices into it. Successively evaluate the full-adder gate list with input indices $a,b,c$ and base index $L$, appending each gate's output to $v$. The resulting list is $v$ followed, in order, by $v_a\lor v_b$, $v_a\land v_b$, $\neg(v_a\land v_b)$, $v_a\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_b$, $(v_a\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_b)\lor v_c$, $(v_a\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_b)\land v_c$, $\neg((v_a\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_b)\land v_c)$, $(v_a\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_b)\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_c$, and $(v_a\land v_b)\lor((v_a\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}v_b)\land v_c)$, where $v_j$ denotes the Boolean value at index $j$.
hypotheses_covered: The indices $a,b,c$ are each less than $L$
